 Follow I've watched every James Bond film - and Josh O'Connor is the shake-up 007 needs
 Sharnaz Shahid Mon, November 16, 2026 at 11:48 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Josh O'Connor (Getty) Having watched every James Bond film since childhood, I've been asked countless times to name my favourite 007. It is an impossible question, and my answer usually shifts depending on my mood. 
 I'm torn between Sean Connery 's charm and Pierce Brosnan 's suave, sharp-suited charisma (who remains my sister's undisputed favourite). Yet, when I look at the films themselves, my all-time favourite instalment is actually 1987's The Living Daylights , starring Timothy Dalton. By that logic, surely Timothy should hold the crown for me?

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That's the beauty - and the difficulty - of the franchise. Every actor brings something entirely different to the tuxedo, making it nearly impossible to settle on one definitive 007. Which is why, as the seemingly endless wait for the next James Bond continues, I find myself hoping that one particular name finally gets the call - Josh O'Connor . 
 Josh O'Connor is among the favourites to be the new James Bond (@ Getty)
 Nothing has been officially announced yet, and there is every chance the producers go in a completely different direction. But if they do hand Josh the keys to the Aston Martin, I truly believe he could end up being the best Bond yet - the one who finally ends the debate for good. 
 How could you not love Josh? Yes, he may not fit the mould of the conventionally chiselled, textbook Hollywood leading man we've come to expect from the 007 rumour mill. But honestly, does that even matter when the man can act as he does? Just look at the sheer range on his CV. 
 Daniel Craig is the last actor to play the iconic Ian Fleming spy (@ Getty Images)
 One minute, he is breaking hearts and capturing the raw vulnerability, awkwardness and royal duty of a young Prince Charles in The Crown ; the next, he is the magnetic, slightly dangerous and alluring Patrick Zweig in Challengers . 
 Timothy Dalton and actress Maryam d'Abo on the set of The Living Daylights (@ Corbis via Getty Images)
 In Challengers , Josh proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that he possesses that intangible screen presence - a mix of roguish charm, unpredictability and underlying edge - that the best Bonds have always relied upon. He doesn't need to flex muscles or rely on brooding stares to command a room; he does it with a look, a wry smile and sheer charisma. 
 Advertisement Advertisement The franchise has never been afraid to take a risk with its leading man. When Daniel Craig was announced as the new Bond in 2005, the reaction was far from universally positive. Critics questioned whether he had the right look for the part, with some dismissing him as too blond and not sufficiently in keeping with the traditional image of 007. 
 Josh O'Connor has starred in Challengers and The Crown (@ Getty Images for Metro-Goldwyn-M)
 Casino Royale quickly silenced many of those doubts, but Daniel Craig's Bond was a moodier, more tortured take on 007. His portrayal ushered in a darker era for the franchise, complete with some major plot twists that took even the most devoted Bond fans by surprise. 
 Of course, there are other contenders who could make a brilliant 007. Callum Turner has all the ingredients the role demands, while Jack Lowden would be equally compelling (though, selfishly, I'd rather he stayed right where he is in his Slow Horses box). 
 But for me, Josh O'Connor offers something different. He has the British pedigree and mischievous spark to bring a fresh perspective to the character - one that teams up Bond's more serious side with the playfulness we've missed. When Amazon finally reveals their new 007, I'll be keeping everything crossed that it's Josh.
